newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS TO PERSEVERE WITH UNDER-FIRE GASCOIGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS TO PERSEVERE WITH UNDER-FIRE GASCOIGNE.

text.p: Glasgow Rangers will persevere with under-fire Paul Gascoigne despite his latest fall from grace.
Gascoigne has not asked for a transfer in the wake of his sending-off against Ajax in Amsterdam on Wednesday and allegations that he assaulted his wife at a Scottish hotel.
The England international has been disciplined for the second dismissal of his Rangers career, although it was not disclosed if the punishment was a fine.
Manager Walter Smith hinted on Thursday he may leave Gascoigne out of Saturday's premier league match against Aberdeen.

"If the problems Paul has had off the field have led to a tension which has meant he can't handle the pressure of playing and has led to him being sent off, then over the next period of time I'll have to look at it," Smith said.
"I'll have to talk with him to see if I consider he can handle playing without over-reacting in the manner he did on Wednesday.
"There has to be a limit to anybody's patience. Understanding can only go so far."
Gascoigne was dismissed by German referee Hellmut Krug for kicking Ajax defender Winston Bogarde in the first half of their European champions' league match.

It left Rangers a man short for more than an hour against the 1995 European champions with Ajax already 1-0 up. The Dutch went on to win 4-1 and Gascoigne received a verbal volley from Rangers skipper Richard Gough.
"He knows himself for an experienced player he has let his team mates down," said Gough. "A few of us had a word with him and he knows himself. He's very upset."
Gascoigne will miss the October 30 return with Ajax and could be banned for at least two more European games when UEFA decide on his punishment next month.
